text: Eyak is an extinct Na-Dené language, historically spoken by the Eyak people, indigenous to south-central Alaska, near the mouth of the Copper River. text: Hän is an endangered indigenous language of the United States. It belongs to the Eyak-Athabaskan language family. The language is used as a first language by the elderly only. It is not known to be taught in schools.
